statement: No single point in time or place can currently be identified for the origin of Homo sapiens. A major synthesis frames modern human ancestry as unfolding across three overlapping phases (worldwide dispersal and archaic admixture, 40-60 ka; African-based diversification of modern-human ancestry, 60-300 ka; complex separation from archaic lineages, 0.3-1 million years ago), and the "pan-African" model — that sapiens features assembled as a mosaic across a subdivided, gene-flow-connected African population network rather than in a single East African "cradle" — is the majority but not unanimous position.
scholarly_disagreement: Whether the mosaic-trait evidence (e.g. Jebel Irhoud, Omo I/II, Florisbad, Herto) reflects genuinely parallel regional evolutionary processes across Africa, or a single lineage with mosaic trait accumulation and one identifiable structural threshold.

sources.citation: Bergström, A., Stringer, C., Hajdinjak, M., Scerri, E.M.L., Skoglund, P. "Origins of modern human ancestry." Nature 590: 229-237. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03244-5
sources.author: Bergström et al.

sources.citation: Scerri, E.M.L. et al. "Did Our Species Evolve in Subdivided Populations across Africa, and Why Does It Matter?" Trends in Ecology & Evolution 33(8): 582-594.
sources.author: Scerri et al.

interpretations.strongest_case: Fossils from geographically distant African sites (Morocco, Ethiopia, South Africa) all show mixtures of archaic and modern traits at different, overlapping dates, consistent with regional populations connected by sporadic gene flow rather than one point of origin.

interpretations.position: Extended single-African-origin, with mosaic trait accumulation but one identifiable structural threshold (acquisition of neurocranial globularity)

holders.name: Andra Meneganzin, Telmo Pievani & Giorgio Manzi
holders.work: "Pan-Africanism vs. single-origin of Homo sapiens," Evolutionary Anthropology 31(4): 199-212

interpretations.strongest_case: The pan-African model has inferential and terminological weaknesses; the mosaic evidence is real but is better explained by a still-recognizable single lineage than by fully independent parallel regional assembly.
